product: A shared job board so independent design studios can track briefs, files, and approvals in one place.
stage: Building. A first version is planned for five studios.
target_customer: Independent design studios with 2 to 10 people
team_capacity: One founder, about 10 hours a week on sales and marketing.

existing_audience.detail: Studios the founder already works with, including the two interviewed.

competitive_alternatives.why_used: Free, familiar, and clients already use email.
A general work tool many teams already pay for.
Client projects, messages, and files in one place.
Review and approval for video teams.

positioning.statement: Email threads and spreadsheets, or a general work tool the studio configures itself.
A client approval link tied to one file version, with no client account needed.
The studio never builds on the wrong version, and clients approve in one click.
Branding studios with 2 to 10 people that send identity work to clients by email.
Client approval software for design studios.

value_proposition: Send clients one link, get approval on the right version, and stop redoing work.

buyer_roles.cares_about: Not losing paid hours to rework, and keeping clients happy.
A low monthly price with no per-client fee.
Uploading a version and getting a clear yes or notes.

offer.basis: Business plan price, set against public plans of Asana and Basecamp.

offer.price: Assumption: first month free, then 40 per month
offer.basis: Lowers the risk for the first five studios while still asking for payment.

messaging.message: Stop redoing work after a client approves the wrong version.
messaging.proof: One interviewed studio lost two days to a wrong-version approval.

messaging.message: Approve the latest design in one click, no account needed.
messaging.proof: Collect from the first pilot: time from link sent to approval.

channels.fit: Warm, fast, and free. Already holds the first studios.
Studio owners gather at chapter events in person.
Catches studios searching for a client approval tool.
A public list of small studios for direct outreach.
Designers discuss feedback rounds, but self-promotion rules apply.
Buyers compare tools there, but reviews are needed first.

channel_tests.test: Ask every studio contact for an intro to one other studio owner.
Attend two chapter events and book calls with studio owners.
Run ads on client approval searches to a pilot signup page.

weekly_target: Assumption: one new paying studio a week after launch. Once revenue is steady, track weekly percent growth; Paul Graham calls 5-7% a week good during YC.

launch_plan.actions: Build the first version. Ask network contacts for intros. Set up the signup page.
launch_plan.milestone: Five studios agree to the pilot.

launch_plan.actions: Onboard the five studios personally. Run the event and ads tests.
launch_plan.milestone: Each pilot studio sends a real approval.

launch_plan.actions: Convert pilots to paid. Ask each paying studio for one intro.
Review each channel test against its threshold. Keep the best channel and drop the rest.
launch_plan.milestone: One channel chosen for the next quarter.

kpis.measured_how: Calendar and a simple pipeline sheet.
Paying studios divided by studios that finished the pilot.

kpis.kpi: Approvals sent per studio per week

risks.risk: The founder's 10 hours a week go to building, not selling.
risks.response: Block two fixed sales mornings a week.

risks.risk: Ads bring designers, not studio owners.
risks.response: Screen signups by studio size before the pilot.

risks.risk: Studios use the pilot but will not pay.
risks.response: Ask for payment at the end of the free month and record the reason for every no.

assumptions.text: AIGA event costs of 100 for two events, for tickets and travel.
A 40% pilot to paid conversion rate. Not measured yet.
One new paying studio a week after launch.

sources.title: The Bullseye Framework for Getting Traction
